summary: Name is two H (or U) handshapes, one tapping on top of the other twice. It's used in 'my name is' and 'what is your name.'
handshape: H hands (index and middle fingers extended)
movement: Dominant hand taps on top of the non-dominant hand twice
steps: Make an H handshape with both hands: index and middle fingers extended together.
Rest the dominant hand's fingers across the top of the other hand's fingers, forming an X.
note: After NAME, you fingerspell. MY NAME then spell it. Most new learners don't have a name sign yet, and that's completely normal; your fingerspelled name is your name until a Deaf friend gives you one.
mistakes: Tapping once. Two small taps is the noun NAME; a single firm contact can read as the verb 'to name.'

faq.q: How do I sign 'my name is'?
faq.a: MY (flat hand on chest) then NAME, then fingerspell your name. There's no sign for 'is.' See the MY-NAME-IS phrase page.
